jobs.description:
Director of Finance and Operations - Permanent - 19202

About the Opportunity

We are seeking a CPA designated professional to join our client's team on a full-time basis. The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical accounting foundation in a project-based construction environment, along with the leadership skills to take on a broader administrative mandate.

The Director of Finance and Operations is responsible for overseeing all aspects of financial management for a well-established, multi-sector construction group of companies, including corporate accounting, regulatory and financial reporting, budget and forecast preparation, and the development of internal control policies and procedures. This position leads financial risk management, safeguards company assets, and provides the timely, accurate financial insight that guides sound business decisions across the organization. Beyond finance, the role also includes oversight of the company's human resources processes and management of the relationship with its external IT provider, making this a key administrative leadership position.

Duties include but are not limited to:
Prepare head office overhead budgets in consultation with management, collecting, analyzing, and consolidating financial data to recommend plans
Achieve financial plan objectives by scheduling expenditures, analyzing variances, and initiating corrective actions
Manage cash flow by forecasting project and corporate cash requirements, monitoring balances, and ensuring liquidity to meet operational and project obligations
Partner with Project Managers, Estimators, and Operations to review project performance and margins, and improve the accuracy of future bids
Prepare and publish timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, reporting on the company's financial condition to senior leadership and external stakeholders
Oversee full-cycle accounting, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and payroll for field and office staff
Monitor the company's externally managed investment portfolio, reconciling third-party statements and reporting on holdings and returns
Oversee project cost accounting, including job costing that tracks labour, equipment, and material costs against project budgets
Lead quarterly work-in-progress (WIP) reviews with Operations and Project Managers, and apply percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
Manage progress billings, subcontractor progress draws, holdbacks/retainage, and lien compliance under the Construction Act
Coordinate regulatory reporting and manage government reporting requirements and tax filings, including CRA and WSIB obligations
Establish, monitor, and enforce financial policies, procedures, and internal controls; coordinate external audits
Manage accounting department operations and staff, including hiring, training, coaching, and performance reviews
Oversee the company's HR function and manage the relationship with its external IT provider

About You

The successful candidate will have the following:
CPA designation preferred
Diploma or degree in Accounting, Business, Finance, or a related discipline
8+ years of combined accounting and finance experience, with proven experience as a financial controller, preferably in the construction industry
Thorough knowledge of accounting principles and procedures, including general ledger functions and the month-end/year-end close process
Demonstrated experience preparing financial statements and regulatory reporting
Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP is a strong asset; familiarity with Procore or similar construction project management software is a plus
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication abilities, with outstanding attention to detail

About the Job

This is an on-site role located in Cambridge, ON
The salary band for this opportunity is $150,000 to $170,000 depending on relevant previous experience, together with a comprehensive benefits package

How to Apply

Please apply by clicking the “Apply Now” button below and follow the instructions to submit your résumé. You can also apply by submitting your résumé directly to amcdougall@lrostaffing.com. If you are already registered with us, please contact your Senior Recruiter. Please quote job 19202
.

Each submission is reviewed by an experienced recruiter to ensure a thoughtful and equitable evaluation of every candidate.

Thank you for your interest in this role. One of our Recruiters will be in touch with you if your profile meets the requirements for the role and the expectations of our clients. Please note that all candidates must be permitted to work in Canada to be considered for this opportunity.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Toronto or Waterloo, hybrid | Full-time | Reports to the CEO

Build the finance function at a fast-growing senior care technology company shipping hardware to 24 countries.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, our consumer product launches in January, and we are preparing our next raise. Every one of those runs on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up in diligence. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast, controls and the numbers behind our next raise, across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

What You'll Own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
The raise: the model, the data room and investor reporting, with you in the room
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and our next raise runs on numbers that hold up in diligence.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

Where this goes

As we raise and scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

What You Get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

Our Commitment

At Pontosense, we are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and accessible to all. We value diversity and believe that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We will work with you to make the necessary accommodations to ensure a fair and positive experience for all applicants.

We strive to provide accessible communication and technology for our employees and customers and always look for ways to improve. If you have any feedback or suggestions on how we can improve accessibility in our workplace, please don't hesitate to contact us.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply for open positions at our company.

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital agency and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across: Digital Product Strategy & Innovation, Digital Marketing Services, Web & Mobile App Development, Data & AI, Cloud Engineering, and Enterprise Technology Modernization.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

Our Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering
will operate remotely in Canada OR be based out of either our Toronto, ON or Vancouver, BC office locations.

The Opportunity

TELUS Digital's Data, AI & Cloud (DAIC) practice is the multidisciplinary engine behind enterprise AI, blending boutique innovation with the breadth of a global services portfolio to help organizations architect, scale, and secure their transformations. Spanning our full family of specialized capabilities, the DAIC practice delivers end-to-end solutions across AI Advisory, AI Solutions, Data & AI Platforms, and Cloud Transformation.

As a premier Google Cloud partner, our Cloud practice is at the forefront of helping enterprises adopt and scale on Google Cloud infrastructure: delivering complex engineering, deployment, and migration programs for some of the largest organizations in Canada and beyond.

The Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering
will define and own the Data Engineering Practice along with its market positioning, P&L, talent, and the quality of work we deliver for clients. This role is for someone who has led data and AI practices before, understands how to turn messy enterprise data estates into strategic assets, and earns trust with C-suite executives through genuine expertise. You will shape how we help clients move from data ambition to durable, AI-ready infrastructure.

This Role Will Have Four Core Anchor Responsibilities

Strategy: Set the practice vision and align Data & AI capabilities to where enterprise demand is heading.
P&L: Own revenue targets, margin, and growth while being accountable for the practice's full commercial performance.
Talent & Culture: Build a practice where data-driven thinking, innovation, and engineering rigour are the baseline.
Client Impact: Act as a trusted advisor to enterprise CxOs navigating data strategy, AI adoption, and governance.

Responsibilities

Define the multi-year vision for the Data Engineering Practice, ensuring our technical capabilities are ahead of the curve for enterprise demand for Data & AI transformation.
Own the full P&L, including pipeline, pricing, delivery margin, and revenue growth, while reporting directly to executive leadership with clear commercial accountability.

Lead the practice's position on ethical AI and data democratisation while making principled, evidence-based bets on where advanced analytics and AI are creating real enterprise value.
Drive investment in reusable IP, data accelerators, and delivery assets that improve consistency, reduce time-to-value, and protect margins at scale.

jobs.title: Director of Product Management, Financial Simulation and Modeling
jobs.description:
About SandboxAQ

SandboxAQ is a high-growth company delivering AI solutions that address some of the world's greatest challenges. The company’s Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) power advances in life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and other sectors.

We are a global team that is tech-focused and includes experts in AI, chemistry, cybersecurity, physics, mathematics, medicine, engineering, and other specialties. The company emerged from Alphabet Inc. as an independent, growth capital-backed company in 2022, funded by leading investors and supported by a braintrust of industry leaders.

At SandboxAQ, we’ve cultivated an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and impact. By investing deeply in our people, we’re building a thriving, global workforce poised to tackle the world's epic challenges. Join us to advance your career in pursuit of an inspiring mission, in a community of like-minded people who value entrepreneurialism, ownership, and transformative impact.

About The Team

The SandboxAQ AI Generation Engine (SAIGE) team’s mission is to accelerate SandboxAQ’s mission of “Deep Impact at Scale”
with a focus on quantitative AI and rapid innovation. More specifically, the SAIGE team aims to:

Build next-generation AI capabilities that establish SandboxAQ as the global pacesetter in quantitative AI.
Identify, incubate, prototype, and launch new AI products for high-potential and longer-term use cases, proving (or disproving) their viability as high-impact, highly profitable business lines.

The SAIGE team operates on the following principles: Prototype with Velocity, Explore Boldly, Fail Smart, Learn Fast, Look Forward, and Share Knowledge.

Our current top priority use case is leveraging AI and LQMs to solve some of the most impactful problems in the Finance and Insurance industries.

The Opportunity

As The Director Of Product Management For The AI Generation Engine (SAIGE), You Will Be The PM Lead For The Team And a Key Partner To Engineering, Research, And User Research. You Will

Own the product strategy and execution for our efforts in Finance & Risk Modeling, partnering closely with financial services and insurance customers to understand their workflows, risk models, and decision-making processes.
Lead rapid prototyping and innovation across a broad range of new ideas and domains, driving 0→1 product discovery, experimentation, and incubation of high-potential use cases.
Operate in a highly ambiguous, fast-changing environment, providing clarity on priorities, making pragmatic trade-offs, and ensuring we ship impactful prototypes and products.

This role is ideal for a seasoned product leader who is energized by uncertainty, enjoys working across disciplines (UXR, engineering, research, business), and is excited to build new AI and quantitative products from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities

Lead product strategy in Finance & Risk Modeling

Own the product vision, roadmap, and execution for our Finance/Risk portfolio, with a focus on financial services and insurance (e.g., portfolio risk, capital modeling, risk analytics, underwriting, and related workflows).
Develop a deep understanding of customer contexts, including current tools, models, and data flows (e.g., portfolio / risk modeling systems, vendor platforms, internal analytics stacks).
Partner with quantitative researchers, ML engineers, and domain experts to translate customer problems into clear product requirements and model/data needs.
Define success metrics and validation strategies to compare our approaches against existing PML/ERM and portfolio views, and to demonstrate differentiated value.

Drive rapid prototyping and 0→1 innovation

Identify, evaluate, and prioritize new AI / LQM use cases across multiple domains (beyond Finance/Risk), from early signals to clearer opportunities.
Lead 0→1 product discovery: problem framing, hypothesis development, lightweight customer validation, and rapid iteration on prototypes.
Work with engineering and research to scope experiments that are small enough to move quickly but meaningful enough to answer key questions.
Establish and champion a rigorous but pragmatic approach to ruthless prioritization, ensuring the team focuses on the highest-impact opportunities.

Build strong customer and stakeholder relationships

Serve as a trusted product partner to senior stakeholders at key customers (e.g., heads of risk, portfolio managers, actuaries, CROs), speaking credibly about risk models, scenarios, and portfolio decisions.
Lead customer conversations from initial discovery through pilot definition and ongoing adoption, connecting customer needs to the SAIGE roadmap.
Communicate progress, learnings, and recommendations clearly to internal and external stakeholders, including executives.

Essential Skills & Experience

You are a senior product leader who is comfortable at the intersection of AI, quantitative modeling, and financial risk
. You thrive in ambiguity, enjoy working closely with deeply technical teams, and can just as easily go deep on models and data as you can on customer needs and business outcomes. You are proactive, low-ego, and collaborative, and you don’t need rigid structure to have impact.

10+ years of product management experience, with substantial time spent on complex B2B or platform products; at least several years operating at a senior / staff / principal / director level (e.g., L7-equivalent scope).
Deep Experience in financial services and/or insurance, especially in one or more of:
Risk modeling (e.g., portfolio risk, capital modeling, asset-liability management, market/credit risk, or insurance risk)
Financial simulation or scenario analysis
Portfolio analytics or decision support tools

Demonstrated ability to work closely with quantitative and engineering teams:
Past experience in building AI / ML products or capabilities
Comfortable discussing models, data pipelines, and trade-offs with engineers and researchers.
Able to translate between technical details and customer/business value.

Proven track record of 0→1 product work:
Identifying new opportunities and shaping them from idea to prototype and early product.
Working through high ambiguity, incomplete information, and changing constraints.

Strong ruthless prioritization skills: can define clear frameworks, make hard trade-offs, and say “no” to good ideas to focus on the best ones.
Exceptional customer-facing skills:
Confident leading discovery and roadmap conversations with senior stakeholders.
Skilled at uncovering real needs behind stated requirements and pressure-testing problem statements.

Demonstrated ability to drive execution without heavy process or structure:
Self-directed, proactive, and comfortable creating structure where needed rather than waiting for it.
Experience in environments with shifting priorities and evolving strategies.

Strong collaboration and communication:
Experience working tightly with UXR, design, engineering, and research.
Clear written and verbal communication across technical and non-technical audiences.

Alignment with SandboxAQ values and the SAIGE principles around rapid prototyping, learning, and shared ownership.

Highly Desired Skills & Experience

Direct experience building products involving AI / ML, foundational models, quantitative models, or LLM/agentic systems.
Hands-on exposure to risk tools and vendor platforms (e.g., risk engines, portfolio analytics systems, or modeling platforms used in insurance and financial services).
Experience in both:
A high-growth startup or new product incubation context, and
A large, complex environment (e.g., Big Tech, major financial institution), giving you a strong sense of how to navigate stakeholders and scale impact.

Educational background in a quantitative or technical field (e.g., computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, engineering, finance, or similar).

If you’re excited by the idea of shaping the future of quantitative AI, building products with real impact in finance and insurance (and possibly other domains), and leading 0→1 innovation in a highly cross-functional team, we’d love to hear from you.

Why Join Us?

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and life outside of work.

Compensation: Competitive base salary, performance-based incentives or bonuses (where applicable), and equity participation.
Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents with generous employer premium contributions, retirement savings with company matching, paid parental leave, and inclusive family-building benefits.
Work-Life Balance: Flexible paid time off, company-wide seasonal breaks, and support for flexible work arrangements that enable sustainable performance.
Career Development: Opportunities for continuous learning and growth through on-the-job development, cross-functional collaboration, and access to internal learning and development programs.

SandboxAQ Welcomes All

We are committed to fostering a culture of belonging and respect, where diverse perspectives are actively sought and valued. Our multidisciplinary environment provides ample opportunity for continuous growth - working alongside humble, empowered, and ambitious colleagues ready to tackle epic challenges.

Equal Employment Opportunity
: All qualified applicants will receive consideration regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status.

Accommodations
: We provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities in job application procedures for open roles. If you need such an accommodation, please let a member of our Recruiting team know.

jobs.title: AVP, Financial Risk Management
jobs.description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count?

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

Overview

The role supports the Financial Risk function within MUFG Canada Risk Management, with a focus on the production, analysis, governance and continuous enhancement of liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and interest rate risk in the banking book reporting. Reporting to the Financial Risk Vice President, the incumbent is responsible for preparing and maintaining recurring risk reports, supporting ECL and portfolio credit risk analysis, monitoring risk appetite and limit metrics, maintaining EUC and procedure documentation, and assisting with committee materials for IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk and Market Risk governance forums. The role requires excellent technical capability, including advanced data analysis, Excel/Power Query/VBA automation, source-data reconciliation, AI literacy and the ability to responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools to improve reporting efficiency, data quality, trend analysis, control effectiveness and management insight. The incumbent must demonstrate strong knowledge of the underlying risk metrics, data sources such as OVS extracts, Bloomberg and internal reporting files, and the ability to translate complex technical outputs into clear, audit-ready commentary and management materials.

Key Accountabilities

Risk reporting, analytics and governance support - responsibilities include:

Prepare, analyze and maintain recurring Financial Risk reports across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including Liquidity Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Limit Dashboard, Liquidity Stress Testing, daily and monthly liquidity monitoring, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, portfolio concentration, IFRS 9 ECL, Watchlist inputs, Risk Appetite metrics and interest rate risk analytics.
Compile and validate source data from OVS extracts, Bloomberg, internal risk files, Treasury reports, Middle Office data, Finance inputs, facility and commitment data, exposure reports and locally maintained EUC tools to support recurring production and independent review of risk metrics.
Support the preparation of IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk, Market Risk and other governance materials by compiling metrics, drafting commentary, preparing exhibits, explaining drivers, documenting assumptions and ensuring materials are accurate, complete and delivered within required timelines.
Perform review and challenge of report outputs, investigate material movements or exceptions, document rationale, reconcile data back to source systems, and escalate breaches, data issues or control concerns in accordance with applicable procedures.

Support for stakeholders - responsibilities include:

Coordinate with Treasury, Middle Office, Finance, Operations, Compliance, business lines, regional risk teams and Head Office to obtain data, validate assumptions, clarify methodology, and support timely completion of Financial Risk deliverables.
Provide support, oversight and guidance to first line and independent risk monitoring functions on risk reporting, risk appetite monitoring, limit usage, breach escalation and remediation tracking.
Support audit, regulatory and internal review requests by maintaining clear evidence, audit trails, version logs, approvals and supporting documentation for recurring reporting processes.
Monitor relevant regulatory, Head Office and regional risk requirements and assist in translating them into local policies, procedures, controls, testing approaches and reporting processes.
Support the review and enhancement of local risk policies, procedures, EUC documentation and user manuals, including documentation for EWI, liquidity limits, LST, market risk reporting, RFR-linked submissions and ECL processes.
Assist with annual recalibration and methodology review processes for liquidity risk metrics, EWI thresholds, LST assumptions, local limits and other Financial Risk measures, including coordination with ALRMO, Head Office and first line stakeholders.
Identify opportunities to automate, streamline and strengthen recurring reports, tracking logs, confirmations and control processes while maintaining appropriate governance, documentation and change management.

Technical Skills

Excellent technical skills, including advanced Microsoft Excel capability with complex formulas, Power Query, pivot tables, data validation, reconciliations, financial modelling, VBA/macros and automation techniques used to streamline recurring risk reporting processes.
Strong knowledge of liquidity risk metrics and reporting, including Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Stress Testing, liquidity limits, limit utilization, funds position, cash-flow analysis, contingency funding plan inputs, liquidity risk appetite measures, threshold recalibration and breach/escalation monitoring.
Strong knowledge of market risk metrics and analytics, including VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity analysis, limit monitoring, market data validation, rate and spread movements, exposure drivers and recurring market risk reporting packages.
Strong knowledge of credit risk and ECL analytics, including IFRS 9 ECL, exposure and commitment utilization, portfolio concentration, industry and obligor analysis, facility data, credit exposure trends and credit risk appetite reporting.
Working knowledge of IRRBB concepts and tools, including interest rate sensitivity, earnings and economic value perspectives, repricing profile analysis, scenario-based impacts, assumptions review and coordination with regional or Head Office stakeholders on IRRBB methodology and tool development.
Ability to source, extract, reconcile and analyze data from multiple internal and external risk systems, Treasury and Middle Office files, Finance inputs, facility and commitment reports, shared-drive repositories, SharePoint sites and locally maintained EUC tools.

jobs.title: Director, Client Strategy
jobs.description:
If this post is up, we are still hiring—even if LinkedIn says applications are no longer accepted.

Position:
Director of Client Strategy
Type of Role:
Full time, remote anywhere in Canada
Reports To:
Managing Director
Compensation:
$115,000 - $130,000 CAD + performance pay
On Target Earnings (OTE):
>$150,000 CAD

About The Company BuildGood is a fundraising growth agency. We help nonprofits change the way they find new donors, retain them longer, and grow lifetime value, building a system that creates moments of generosity from first-time giver to legacy leaver.

Our approach is rooted in understanding why people give. Generosity grows when people feel motivated—when giving supports their identity, creates a sense of connection, and makes supporters feel competent and effective in their giving. We design fundraising systems around building donor motivation and leading first-time donors to become committed supporters.

We partner with nonprofits across North America to grow durable revenue, from donor acquisition and direct mail to digital fundraising, retention, and mid-level giving. Our work blends brand and direct response.

Is This Job For You? Do you get fired up about turning client relationships into long-term, high-impact partnerships?

Do you understand what it takes to grow fundraising and be responsible for revenue targets, and know
how to help others turn that understanding into stronger strategies and better results?

Are you energized by leading a team of Strategists and Account Managers, challenging their thinking, building their confidence, and helping them manage client relationships well?

Can you look at a client’s fundraising program, identify the biggest opportunities, and help your team build a clear plan for growth?

Are you comfortable leading important client conversations, addressing concerns directly, and making the case for renewing or expanding a partnership?

And do you want to build a high-performance client strategy function at a fundraising agency that’s genuinely changing how nonprofits grow?

We’re looking for someone who combines deep fundraising knowledge with strong account management and people leadership. You’ll lead the team that owns our client accounts, set the standard for strategy and client experience, and take responsibility for keeping and growing those partnerships.

What We Offer A workplace that values your need for autonomy, competence and connection
An entrepreneurial culture that places a premium on rigor and accountability
A teamwork environment built on both humour and challenging each other to continuously improve in our craft
Meaningful work that directly influences how organizations grow
Attendance at the Build Good Summit, Canada’s premiere fundraising conference
Work from home anywhere in Canada
4 weeks vacation
Summer Fridays (Fridays off in June, July, and August)
Generous professional development budget
Group Retirement Savings Plan (GRSP)
Flexible Spending Account (HSA)
Performance pay based on meeting goals and targets

What You’ll Do

You will own the strategy and execution for how our client team grows and protects BuildGood’s client portfolio. Your focus will be on client success, retention, renewals, expansion, and the profitability of each account—ensuring our work delivers measurable fundraising results, gives clients a clear reason to deepen their partnership with us, and generates a healthy profit for BuildGood.

You will set the direction for BuildGood’s client strategy function and lead the team responsible for putting it into practice. You’ll manage our Fundraising Strategists and Account Managers, set the standard for fundraising strategy and account management, and own all renewals and expansion across the client portfolio.

Every account will have a clear growth plan that connects the client’s fundraising goals with the work, investment, and decisions needed to achieve them. You’ll help your team build those plans, hold them accountable for progress, and ensure clients understand the value of our work and where the partnership can go next.

You’ll lead through your team while participating directly in strategic reviews, important client conversations, renewals, and escalations. You’ll work closely with the Managing Director, who provides commercial leadership and sets pricing, margin, and other business parameters.

Your main responsibilities:
Lead, coach, and develop BuildGood’s Fundraising Strategists and Account Managers through regular 1:1s, account reviews, clear performance expectations, and professional development.
Review and challenge the fundraising strategy across the client portfolio. Review and challenge recommendations to ensure they reflect donor insights, performance data, and the client’s goals.
Own and iterate the Total Fundraising Review & Revenue Roadmap, our flagship diagnostic, forecasting and planning process at the beginning of each new client relationship built on our Brand → Demand → Expand and Fundraising FlywheelTM IP.
Work closely with the Creative Director to ensure the work we deliver is outstanding—grounded in a strong fundraising strategy, built around donor insights, and executed with exceptional craft. Together, review key campaigns and deliverables, challenge work that falls short, and coach the team toward a consistently high standard.
Ensure every account has a documented growth plan covering fundraising priorities, measurable goals, recommended investment, renewal timing, relationship risks, and opportunities to expand the partnership.
Make annual planning and Quarterly Fundraising Reviews the foundation of account management, ensuring each review leads to clear recommendations, decisions, and next steps.
Hold the team accountable for executing account plans, monitoring results, and adjusting strategy when performance or circumstances change.
Own renewal planning and execution across the portfolio. Maintain a clear renewal calendar and forecast, prepare the team, and lead renewal conversations within the commercial parameters agreed with the Managing Director.
Identify and advance opportunities to expand client partnerships where additional BuildGood services or investment would help the client achieve its fundraising goals.
Monitor account health using fundraising performance, client feedback, engagement, and relationship strength. Act early when results, trust, or renewal prospects are at risk.
Serve as the senior escalation point for client challenges. Lead the response, coordinate the right people, communicate clearly with the client, and follow through to resolution.
Ensure client strategies, presentations, and reports are clear, credible, and useful. Help the team explain what happened, what it means, and what should happen next.
Partner with creative, data, digital, production, and project management leaders to ensure work follows the agreed strategy and meets client expectations.
Own the profitability of each client account. Monitor account revenue, delivery costs, scope, and resource use against agreed profit targets. Address scope creep and unprofitable work early, and work with the Managing Director on pricing, staffing, or scope changes needed to protect profit while delivering excellent client results.
Partner with the Managing Director to ensure commitments made during the sales process carry through into onboarding and account planning.
Hire and onboard members of the client strategy team, and build consistent practices that help the team deliver strong work with greater independence.
Establish regular client feedback and use it to improve account management, service quality, and the client experience.
Serve on BuildGood’s Leadership Team, participating in weekly leadership meetings and quarterly in-person sessions.

Skills & Experience Significant experience in nonprofit fundraising strategy, direct-response marketing, and fundraising agency account management, typically gained over 7 or more years.
At least 5 years of experience managing and developing a team, including setting expectations, coaching performance, hiring, and handling difficult conversations.
Deep knowledge of direct-response fundraising across disciplines and channels, with the ability to connect acquisition, retention, monthly, mid-level, and legacy giving into a coherent growth strategy.
Demonstrated success managing client relationships and leading account planning, renewals, and expansion.
Strong analytical judgment: you can interpret fundraising performance, identify the underlying issues, and turn findings into clear recommendations.
The ability to evaluate other people’s strategies and coach them toward stronger thinking and better work.
A consultative approach: you ask good questions, make complex information understandable, and present recommendations with confidence.
Credibility with senior nonprofit leaders and experience navigating concerns, competing priorities, and difficult client situations.
Commercial awareness: you understand how scope, pricing, and resource decisions affect account profitability.
Experience using CRM and project management tools to maintain visibility into account plans, commitments, risks, and renewal opportunities.
Significant agency experience is required.

The Hiring Process

Send an email to hr@buildgood.com
Subject Line: Application – Director of Client Strategy
In the email, briefly share why you want to work with BG, why it’s a good fit, and a link to a song that gets you excited about fundraising
If you have LinkedIn, include a link to your profile
Attach your resume (we’ll read it) and don’t attach a cover letter (we won’t read it)
In addition, fill out this screening form. If you haven’t filled out this form, we consider the application incomplete.

We can’t guarantee that we will get back to every single applicant. If you have not heard from us two weeks after you apply, please assume that you were not included in the final field of applicants.

new_jobs.description:
Director of Finance and Operations - Permanent - 19202

About the Opportunity

We are seeking a CPA designated professional to join our client's team on a full-time basis. The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical accounting foundation in a project-based construction environment, along with the leadership skills to take on a broader administrative mandate.

The Director of Finance and Operations is responsible for overseeing all aspects of financial management for a well-established, multi-sector construction group of companies, including corporate accounting, regulatory and financial reporting, budget and forecast preparation, and the development of internal control policies and procedures. This position leads financial risk management, safeguards company assets, and provides the timely, accurate financial insight that guides sound business decisions across the organization. Beyond finance, the role also includes oversight of the company's human resources processes and management of the relationship with its external IT provider, making this a key administrative leadership position.

Duties include but are not limited to:
Prepare head office overhead budgets in consultation with management, collecting, analyzing, and consolidating financial data to recommend plans
Achieve financial plan objectives by scheduling expenditures, analyzing variances, and initiating corrective actions
Manage cash flow by forecasting project and corporate cash requirements, monitoring balances, and ensuring liquidity to meet operational and project obligations
Partner with Project Managers, Estimators, and Operations to review project performance and margins, and improve the accuracy of future bids
Prepare and publish timely monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, reporting on the company's financial condition to senior leadership and external stakeholders
Oversee full-cycle accounting, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, and payroll for field and office staff
Monitor the company's externally managed investment portfolio, reconciling third-party statements and reporting on holdings and returns
Oversee project cost accounting, including job costing that tracks labour, equipment, and material costs against project budgets
Lead quarterly work-in-progress (WIP) reviews with Operations and Project Managers, and apply percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
Manage progress billings, subcontractor progress draws, holdbacks/retainage, and lien compliance under the Construction Act
Coordinate regulatory reporting and manage government reporting requirements and tax filings, including CRA and WSIB obligations
Establish, monitor, and enforce financial policies, procedures, and internal controls; coordinate external audits
Manage accounting department operations and staff, including hiring, training, coaching, and performance reviews
Oversee the company's HR function and manage the relationship with its external IT provider

About You

The successful candidate will have the following:
CPA designation preferred
Diploma or degree in Accounting, Business, Finance, or a related discipline
8+ years of combined accounting and finance experience, with proven experience as a financial controller, preferably in the construction industry
Thorough knowledge of accounting principles and procedures, including general ledger functions and the month-end/year-end close process
Demonstrated experience preparing financial statements and regulatory reporting
Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP is a strong asset; familiarity with Procore or similar construction project management software is a plus
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication abilities, with outstanding attention to detail

About the Job

This is an on-site role located in Cambridge, ON
The salary band for this opportunity is $150,000 to $170,000 depending on relevant previous experience, together with a comprehensive benefits package

How to Apply

Please apply by clicking the “Apply Now” button below and follow the instructions to submit your résumé. You can also apply by submitting your résumé directly to amcdougall@lrostaffing.com. If you are already registered with us, please contact your Senior Recruiter. Please quote job 19202
.

Each submission is reviewed by an experienced recruiter to ensure a thoughtful and equitable evaluation of every candidate.

Thank you for your interest in this role. One of our Recruiters will be in touch with you if your profile meets the requirements for the role and the expectations of our clients. Please note that all candidates must be permitted to work in Canada to be considered for this opportunity.

Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.
